comment: Cases for tests/trace/check.py. Each one runs a program under a VP with a fixed set of
flags and compares the resulting trace against reference/<name>.json.
A case with "ci": false is left out by --ci. It needs something the CI image does not
have (cross compiler with a C library).

cases.name: minimal
cases.comment: Five instructions. The smallest case that produces a tree at all.

cases.name: default
cases.comment: The general case: arithmetic, branches and a loop.

cases.name: memory
cases.comment: Pins the load and store bookkeeping: access counts, offset sums and the memory dependency edges.

cases.name: output-dep
cases.comment: Pins the output and anti dependency edges, which no other case reaches.

cases.name: prefix
cases.comment: Pins the true_weight counting, where overlapping windows sharing a prefix must not be counted twice.

cases.name: basic-c
cases.comment: A compiled C program rather than hand written assembly, so the instruction mix is realistic. Its array initializers make the compiler emit memcpy and memset, so unlike the other cases it needs a cross compiler with a C library

cases.name: depth-4
cases.comment: A second depth. Depth changes which windows exist, so running two depths catches a change that only shows up at one of them.

cases.name: basic-platform
cases.comment: The basic platform rather than tiny32. It has peripherals and a different memory map.

cases.name: rv64
cases.comment: The 64 bit ISS on the same program source, so the two architectures cannot drift apart unnoticed.

cases.name: no-trace
cases.comment: The same program as basic-c with --no-trace. It writes no file, so the counters and the register file are the check: running without recording must not change what the program does.

cases.name: clint
cases.comment: A program that reaches the CLINT and the syscall region. Both sat inside the memory range on tiny32 until 2026-09-29, and the bus answers with the first port that contains an address, so memory hid them and this program never terminated. It runs in 20 ms; if it hangs, the memory map overlaps a peripheral again.
